comment: The rate of skipped display slots (checks.pacing.max_late_frac) is the one pacing number that depends on the machine; the other pacing checks (no stall, cadence, no hitch, steady latency, vsync) are the same everywhere. On this rig e2e_openxr_probe (1800 frames) measured 2.46 % and 2.52 % in two runs, all of it made before the encoder (the same 2.5 % at the host's send): the app or the boundary pick had nothing ready for that slot. It measured about 0 % on 2026-10-08/09, before the Oct 10 pacing redesign. The ceiling is twice today's value: a regression on this rig still fails. client_p99_ms and intake_p99_ms are the one-skipped-slot values (22 ms) with margin.

rigs.name: RTX 3080 Ti Laptop
rigs.fg_comment: Frame generation with the neural synthesis (the default since 1.4.2) on this GPU, 2026-11-24 (results 20261124T125845Z, T130120Z, T130357Z): a neural run takes 7.7 ms at x2 and 10.0 ms at x3 at the lab's 1760x1600 eye (1.2-1.8 ms on the RTX 5090), the GPU at full clocks and about 45 % busy, so the generator handles 27 of 45 pairs a second at x2 (stream 65 fps) and 15.5 of 30 at x3 (55.9 fps); edge synthesis holds 89.9 fps on the same rig. This GPU does not hold x2 / x3 at that size with neural: its baseline is the observed value with a margin (stream fps 90 % of it, the neural run 115 % of it), so a regression on this rig still fails. The 5090's bar (0.95 of the display rate) stays the scenarios' own. e2e_fg_neural_small (1248x1120 eye) holds the rate on this GPU (89.1 / 88.5 fps, 5.2 ms a run): it keeps the 0.95 bar and only bounds the run time.
